discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 101733
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
1233 PM EST Tue Nov 10 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Sunshine today with highs into the low-mid 60s. 

- A low pressure system moves through Wednesday afternoon into 
  Wednesday night with a period of rain.

- Lake effect showers impact areas mainly west of US-31 in nw IN
  and far sw MI Thursday through Friday night. Snow may mix in 
  by late Thursday night into Friday morning. 

- Below normal temperatures Thursday through this weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 226 AM EST Tue Nov 10 2026

Another pleasant and mild day today despite a weak, washed out, 
frontal passage as another shortwave bypasses well north through the 
northern and eastern Great Lakes. This flattened, high latitude, 
flow then gives way to a full-latitude longwave trough over the 
Eastern CONUS by the second half of this week. This transition will 
drive a compact shortwave southeast through the area Wednesday 
afternoon-evening. The associated frontal wave and pacific moisture 
origins will bring chances (50-80%) for a period of rain during this 
time, with a few heavier convective elements possible south of US-30 
near the sfc low track and steeper mid level lapse rates. 

Colder air wraps in behind this low Thursday into Friday as several 
more shortwave impulses drop through the region in deep northerly 
flow. A secondary trough and steepening lapse rates with the cold 
pool will keep chances for scattered rain showers in the forecast 
area-wide into Thursday. This chilly northerly flow (850 mb temps 
fall to near -5C) brings about a full transition to lake effect rain 
otherwise Thursday through Friday night. Favorable long lake 
fetch/convergence and thermal parameters will allow for more 
organized lake effect banding to settle into our northerly flow lake 
belts at times, mainly west of US-31 in far nw IN (especially 
LaPorte/Starke counties Thursday night-Friday). Wet-bulb zero 
heights may collapse to less than 1 kft later Thursday night into 
Friday morning just inland from the lake. The NBM and ensemble 
guidance hint at the potential for slushy snow accums here (mainly 
LaPorte/Starke Ct). Confidence is low given lingering uncertainties 
regarding low level flow trajectories, warm lake and marginally cold 
nature to the incoming air mass.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z WEDNESDAY/...
Issued at 1227 PM EST Tue Nov 10 2026

Most, if not all, of the forecast period will see light winds
and VFR conditions. A window of concern does exist with regards
to some fog/stratus potential late tonight into Wed morning.
Guidance varies on coverage and nature (shallow vs more
widespread). Have opted to leave out of TAFs for now, but at
least some MVFR vsbys may need to be added in later forecasts. 

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Steinwedel
AVIATION...Fisher

spc.summary: Thunderstorms capable of isolated hail are possible along the Middle to Upper Texas Coast tonight.
spc.text:
SPC AC 101619

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1019 AM CST Tue Nov 10 2026

   Valid 101630Z - 111200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS THE
   MIDDLE TO UPPER TX COAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms capable of isolated hail are possible along the Middle
   to Upper Texas Coast tonight.

   ...TX Coast...
   Recent surface analysis places an inverted trough just off the Lower
   TX Coast. Warm-air advection near this trough is supporting an area
   of showers and thunderstorms. 12Z BRO and CRP soundings show a deep
   and moist boundary layer atop relatively cool mid-level temperatures
   (around -9 to -10 deg C at 500 mb). Enhanced mid-level flow exists
   above 700 mb as well, contributing to moderate shear within the
   cloud bearing layer. These factors could support isolated updrafts
   capable of marginally severe hail through the early afternoon.
   Weakening warm-air advection should lead to weakening thunderstorm
   coverage and intensity during the late afternoon/early evening. 

   The weak vorticity maximum currently over the TX South Plains will
   drift southeastward today, interacting with this more moist and
   buoyant airmass along the coast around 00Z. Ascent associated with
   this wave coupled with modest warm-air advection will likely result
   in increasing thunderstorm coverage after 00Z. Mid-level
   temperatures will cool slightly as well, supporting an increase in
   the elevated buoyancy across the region. Mid-level flow throughout
   this layer will remain strong, with cloud-bearing layer shear over
   50 kt. These environmental conditions appear supportive of
   marginally severe hail within any of the more persistent updrafts.

   ...Elsewhere...
   Occasional lightning flashes may occur with low-topped convection
   that will move quickly east-northeastward across parts of coastal WA
   today in tandem with another mid-level shortwave trough, but very
   weak instability will limit the severe threat with this activity.
   Late afternoon thunderstorms are also possible within the moist
   confluent flow over the central/southern FL Peninsula.

   A few flashes are also possible near the center of the TX vorticity
   maximum over central/north-central TX this afternoon/early evening.
   Thunderstorm coverage in this region is currently expected to be
   less than 10 percent.

   ..Mosier/Halbert-K.. 11/10/2026

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.summary: Thunderstorms with isolated severe wind gusts and perhaps a tornado or two will be possible on Wednesday across parts of the lower Ohio and western Tennessee Valleys.
spc.text:
SPC AC 101716

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1116 AM CST Tue Nov 10 2026

   Valid 111200Z - 121200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PORTIONS
   OF THE LOWER OHIO AND WESTERN TENNESSEE VALLEYS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms with isolated severe wind gusts and perhaps a tornado
   or two will be possible on Wednesday across parts of the lower Ohio
   and western Tennessee Valleys.

   ... Synopsis ...

   The midlevel flow is expected to amplify on Wednesday as a shortwave
   trough digs southeast across the Mississippi Valley. This digging
   trough will help carve out an eastern US long-wave trough at the
   same time as a ridge builds across the western US. 

   At the surface a weak surface low will move east from Illinois
   toward eastern Ohio. To the southwest of this low a surface cold
   front will push south and east. Low-level moisture will increase
   slightly ahead of the advancing cold front. 


   ... Lower Ohio and western Tennessee Valleys ...

   Ahead on the approaching cold front, diurnal heating will combine
   with increasing surface moisture to result in modest destabilization
   (REFS indicating around 40-60 percent chance MUCAPE at least 500
   J/kg, but less than 10 percent change of exceeding 1000 J/kg) during
   the late afternoon across the area. Scattered thunderstorms will
   likely develop by early evening as the cold front interacts with the
   axis of greater instability. Strong mid-level wind fields may
   support a few strong, perhaps damaging, wind gusts. Additionally,
   forecast low-level wind fields indicate modest turning with height
   across the region, which may support a brief window for a tornado or
   two. This marginal tornado threat would be highly conditional on the
   quality of the low-level moisture and degree of instability that is
   realized.

   ..Marsh.. 11/10/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 100823

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0223 AM CST Tue Nov 10 2026

   Valid 121200Z - 131200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe thunderstorms are forecast across the U.S. Thursday and
   Thursday night.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   An upper-level trough will move across the eastern U.S. on Thursday,
   as a cold front advances eastward through the Atlantic coastal
   states. During the day, thunderstorms will be possible along and
   ahead of the front from the Mid-Atlantic southward into far eastern
   North Carolina. Instability is expected to be too weak for a severe
   threat. Elsewhere across the continental U.S., no severe threat is
   forecast Thursday and Thursday night.

   ..Broyles.. 11/10/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
